Excellent game ruined by a dev with a huge ego. Such a shame that we will never see multiplayer or the roadmap's content, ever.

After several years and over 776 hours I have finally 100%ed Forager. I wholeheartedly recommend this game, the rest will be some light reminiscence. I first began playing this game a long time ago, on my Switch (I think). At some point I got it on my tablet and, eventually, a computer. I used to play it a ton and would AFK every night, causing my high playtime, but I never fully finished it. This was due to a lack of dedication. It took me around seven and a half hours once I set to doing it, from my best save file. It is somewhat weird to have it done, but it was very fun. I hope that, someday, Hop Frog returns, as it seems as though he has entirely abandoned the game and social media. Please, Hop Frog, give us more content, I beg you. Also, I used to watch Dangerously Funny play this game, his videos are awesome, go watch them.

It was a ready good game when it was first released, however, the road map was abandoned and the dev just went MIA so don't buy this game expecting a finish product. Overall, gameplay was still entertaining to last me a few weeks. BTW, the comics in the game indicating that it was a solo project is not real, don't believe what he stated.
This game as so much potential on the levels of terraria and minecraft, Its a real shame what happened with the lead dev.

Started playing just to see what the game was about.
A few hours later I’m collecting rocks, mining everything in sight and somehow still telling myself “I’ll stop after this one upgrade.”
Really simple but ridiculously addictive. There’s always something to unlock or upgrade, so it’s very easy to lose track of time.
Would recommend if you like games where you can turn your brain off and just grind.
It’s the kind of game you boot up to relax, only to end up busy with one little thing after another. It’s simple, but oddly hard to stop playing.

This took me 56 hours, to 100% the game, and I have some things to point out.

First of all, the game is REALLY fun, the bouncy and fun pixel art style is really pleasing and the gameplay is (most of the time) thought out and well done. Plus, the music brings the experience to a next level, it just blends right in, its perfect for this game!

On the other hand - and I'll address the elephant in the room, soon - some of this whole '56 hours' has just been me sleeping irl and keeping my game open, when a game REQUIRES you to do that, that's bad design unfortunately, Forager also doesn't have a fully fleshed out endgame, it relies on a LOT of grinding  instead of discovering new things, and some bugs and unintentional 'ways to do it' are found EVERYWHERE.

Well, now, for the BIG thing: This game is dead. I know, barely people play it anymore and the developer has gone somewhere myster

This is what an incremental game needs to be. Yes it has an "end" where upgrades don't matter as much anymore, so any work is just adding a grenade to a mass driver from space, but that's just it. You can go to rediculous levels and dominate the world you're given. I got to lvl 100 in that dungeon to mark it as completed.
30 hours to complete this fun, incremental, top down "fps", terraria x muck, story, puzzle game. It's worth it as it's satisfying.

Open the game for a quick 30 min session and end it, 8 hours later, at 4 am... worth it. 
Great game but has a few bugs here and there (eg. the droids get stuck on the fishing traps when they try to harvest them, they do get unstuck when you get a certain distance away from the traps. But its still annoying). 
Other than that, the game is fantastic. 9/10.

It's a very fun game, but be aware the maker seems to hate his players? Or himself? There is at least one character that's a stand-in for the creator who will appear and ask your character questions that, even if answered correctly, are wrong and result in said creator character abusing you as a player. I played Forager and honestly, it’s super fun. You start small, build farms, craft tools, explore islands, and fight monsters. It can get a bit repetitive if you play a lot, but overall it’s really addictive and satisfying.

🟢 PRO:

   -Extremely addictive gameplay – digging, crafting, farming, and exploring feels endlessly rewarding.

   -Satisfying progression – skill trees, upgrades, and new tools keep you motivated.

   -Colorful, simple graphics – easy on the eyes and perfect for long sessions.

   -Plenty of variety – from farming and cooking to puzzles and combat, there’s always something to do.

🔴 CONTRA:

   -The map can feel repetitive if you stick to the same activity for too long.

   -Inventory management can get tricky, but it’s part of the challenge.

🏁 VERDICT:

9.5/10 – Highly recommended for casual and hardcore players alike.

One of the best and most relaxing experiences I've had in a while. Forager merges survival, crafting and coziness in a beautiful pixel art style full of isles to buy and explore. Every island is full of new adventures, monsters, resources and interesting dungeons. 

I've had a lot of fun playing this game and there is a ton of stuff to do and complete. It's not a hard game nor a very challenging experience, but no less than a great adventure. It gets a bit clunky when you try to play on a controller, as targeting blocks and structures is f*cking mental and you can't change your toolbar unless you click it with your mouse, but hey, it's a fun game.

I remember playing this game when I was a kid, and the idea of being able to create so much from so little inspired me in a way. This game is fairly simplistic when starting it, mine, craft, mine more, and so on. However once you begin to explore more of the world, you realize that many solutions often require out-of-the-box thinking, such as the Galaxy puzzles, as well as figuring out optimal setups for resource farming. Although the endgame can be quite lengthy, and 100%'ing takes a good amount of effort, in the end, it's an accomplishment that you will be proud of. I'm so glad I discovered this gem of a game.
It's an extremely addicting game which always has you thinking of new ways to approach the world around you, and that's what I love so much about Forager, and I'm proud to say that after all these years, I've finally reached 100% feat completion. <3

[h1]Full Review[/h1]
I like sandbox games, and Forager’s cute visuals caught my eye while browsing Steam one day, so I picked it up during a sale. I had some fun, but I always felt like it was missing something. This review aims to clarify that feeling, as well as encourage prospective players toward better game experiences than this.

Gameplay:
Forager is mainly a sandbox survival game, but it draws a lot of inspiration from various other games and genres. The main gameplay loop is harvesting various materials that appear randomly on your island, crafting said materials into more advanced materials, and turning those materials into things needed to progress, such as tool upgrades. As everyone else states. Optimisation is terrible, When you play the game continuously, at about the 1.5 hour mark, the game will drop to 40fps and stay there until you restart. This was manageable but now 8 hours in the game OPENS in 40 fps!!! I've never seen anything like it on a 2D pixel game; using a computer that runs games like satisfactory and helldivers 2 on ultra at a smooth sixty.
